intervention.change: Decoding stop at the first complete answer marker: generation of each plain-prompt answer ends as soon as the first '\boxed{' has its brace-balanced closing '}' or, if earlier, the first line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:' is completed by a newline (vLLM stop on that event, implemented as a logits processor that forces EOS once the marker closes); everything else as in the base_plain_1.0 cell (no prefix, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384). The graded text is the truncated text, so grader v3's last marker is the first marker.

cell.prompt: plain: the standard rlneurons MATH-500 prompt with no prefilled tokens (no cue)
cell.seeds: one sample per problem, per-request seed 1,000,000 + problem_index, as in the T3 cell

intervention.count: Right answers over all 500 MATH-500 problems, grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) on the stopped text against gold; an empty extraction counts wrong; an answer that reaches the 16,384-token cap without a marker counts wrong.

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, v3, vote over 4 samples with ties to the shortest finished sample (the honest unselected-rule figure is 450, vote over 4 after restart, result-5d032f)

intervention.why: The mechanism says the plain register's T 1.0 loss is mostly answers that reach a right first answer and then fail to stop, running on into new answers or invented problems that the last-marker grader v3 reads, so forcing a stop at the first marker should recover roughly its predicted 17 % of the ~260 wrong non-self-opened answers (+~40 over 224, minus a few rows that revise toward the right answer), giving about 250 of 500 in this cell, still far below the cue's best.
